answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before trading or voting, locked through a challenge period. In a cedar-market island, an attacker creating hundreds of sybils must tie up capital in every account; proven abuse forfeits those bonds, while honest agents get theirs back. This does not prove identities are unique, but makes extra influence costly and exposes the attacker to direct financial loss instead of free votes. The timber trade can continue under the same rule.
